title: Analysis of Propaganda in Tweets From Politically Biased Sources

live_model.evidence: Sec. Experiments: "GPT 3.5 turbo, GPT 4, GPT 4 turbo, GPT 4o, GPT 4o-mini... As of August 2024"; Table 2 row "4 turbo .71/.69/.70 .73/.72/.72".

prompt.note: 2A asks the LLM for its own definition of propaganda; 2B embeds the 18 propaganda-technique definitions from Martino et al. 2020 and a fixed 3-way output (propaganda/non-propaganda/not sure); wording not quoted, no appendix found.

claim.metric: F1, Experiment 2B (technique definitions in prompt), row '4 turbo'
claim.location: Table 2 (captioned 'PTC news dataset'), row '4 turbo', 2B F1 column; a second, uncaptioned table with the same layout gives F1=0.63 (2B) elsewhere

data.source: PTC (SemEval-2020 Task 11, public); JMBX, the paper's own annotated political-tweet corpus, stated to be publicly available (Sec. 3)

notes: 200-tweet zero-shot sample (100 propaganda/100 non) run across 8 LLMs under 2 prompt variants. The two results tables' dataset labeling is internally inconsistent (Table 2 says PTC, but the 200-tweet sample is described as drawn from the JMBX corpus), so the exact dataset behind each cell is not fully certain.
